gloss: to sneak in, to steal into

definitions.gloss: to sneak in, to steal into, to slip in secretly
definitions.explanation: To enter a place secretly and without being noticed, often with the intent to do something covert. Can refer to physical intrusion by a person or the gradual, unnoticed arrival of something abstract.

examples.japanese: {泥棒|どろぼう}が{家|いえ}に{忍|しの}び{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: A thief snuck into the house.

examples.japanese: {猫|ねこ}がいつの{間|ま}にか{部屋|へや}に{忍|しの}び{込|こ}んでいた。
examples.english: A cat had slipped into the room without anyone noticing.

examples.japanese: {夜中|よなか}にこっそり{学校|がっこう}の{校舎|こうしゃ}に{忍|しの}び{込|こ}んだことがある。
examples.english: I once snuck into the school building in the middle of the night.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound verb combining {忍|しの}ぶ (to endure; to hide) and {込|こ}む (to go in deeply). Emphasizes stealth and secrecy. Common in crime reporting, mystery fiction, and everyday stories about entering somewhere covertly.

GRAMMAR:
Godan verb ending in む. Takes に to mark the destination: Xに{忍|しの}び{込|こ}む.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {家|いえ}に{忍|しの}び{込|こ}む: to sneak into a house
- {部屋|へや}に{忍|しの}び{込|こ}む: to steal into a room
- こっそり{忍|しの}び{込|こ}む: to sneak in secretly
- {夜中|よなか}に{忍|しの}び{込|こ}む: to sneak in at night
